messages:
Elena: RFC follow-up: propose a lightweight "service anchor" pattern to peel stable capabilities (kv-cache, session-router, prefix-cache) out of the hotpath. Idea: tiny stable shim (stitch adapter) + clear ownership + incremental canaries. summary below, want quick concerns.

Jon: high level +1. main perf worry: extra hop on hotpath.

Elena: mitigation: two adapter modes - inline (library shim, zero-network hop) for tight-latency slices, and remote RPC for admin/observability. keep wire format tiny and versioned.

Priya: migration story? caches are messy.

Elena: phased canary: sample-based dual-read (1%->5%->25%->100%) + background reconciliation. keys get version prefix during transition. if divergence > 1% we roll back.

Theo: also need soft-fallback in shim so callers can route to legacy path on error spikes. circuit-breaker + fallback config.

InfraBot: Created issue infra#4301 - "anchors: spike and perf harness"

Jon: testing: provide perf harness with synthetic session churn and TTL expiry patterns. want baseline numbers for inline vs remote.

Priya: contract surface area suggestion: Read/Get, Write/Put, Update/Patch, Observe/Stats, Admin(Freeze/Drain). Keeps adapters small.

Elena: agreed. proto interface (pseudo):
StitchAdapter.get(key) -> value|null; StitchAdapter.put(key,value,opts) -> ok; StitchAdapter.stats() -> {hits,misses,divergence_sample}; admin.freeze()/drain().

Theo: tracing/metrics: include anchor_id and adapter_version in spans. add divergence_sample gauge and canary_step tag.

Jon: operational guardrails: owners must publish runbook + SLA, and anchors can't accept >X% production traffic until reconciliation job proves <0.5% divergence for 24h.

Priya: action items: Elena PoC adapter + perf baseline (next Tue), Jon test harness (next Wed), Theo runbook + dashboard template (EOW). I'll start drafting contract proto today.

Elena: thanks. I'll write RFC follow-up doc with minimal contract, canary steps, perf targets, and rollback checklist. Small, reversible changes only. :thumbsup:
